name: Grand Hotel Les Trois Rois
positioning: Historic grand hotel on the Rhine in the heart of Basel's Old Town, on a site first mentioned as the inn 'Drei Konige' in 1681
best_for: Travelers who want a central riverside base in Basel's Old Town
Food lovers drawn to Cheval Blanc by Peter Knogl
Guests who enjoy hotels with a long, storied history

facts.text: The hotel sits right on the Rhine, in the heart of Basel's Old Town.
The inn 'Drei Konige', meaning Three Kings, was first mentioned in 1681.
In 1754 innkeeper Johann Christoph Im Hof mounted three wooden king figures on the inn's facade.
In 1797 General Napoleon Bonaparte stopped at the inn while passing through and was received with a state reception.
Basel architect Amadeus Merian was commissioned to design the new building that replaced the old inn.
The new hotel 'Des Trois Rois' opened its doors on February 16, 1844.
Empress Michiko of Japan, writer James Joyce and artist Pablo Picasso were all guests of the hotel.
The Thomas Straumann family acquired the hotel in 2004.
Rooms and suites are in the historic main building at Blumenrain 8 and the newly redesigned head building at Blumenrain 2.
The hotel held 3 Keys in the Michelin Guide in 2025.
Brasserie Les Trois Rois held 15 GaultMillau points in 2025.
The Seijaku Wellbeing area is reserved exclusively for hotel guests.

highlights.text: Cheval Blanc by Peter Knogl held 3 stars in the Michelin Guide in 2025.
In June 2025, after a two-year transformation by Herzog & de Meuron, the listed head building at Blumenrain 2 was unveiled.
Seijaku, a wellbeing area built around Japanese mindfulness culture, sits high above the city's rooftops in a building designed by Herzog & de Meuron.
Restaurant Banks at Blumenrain 2 offers social dining with a European-Asian flair.
The Council, the hotel's cigar lounge, has two fireplaces and 570 handcrafted tiles.

considerations.text: The interiors are a tribute to Belle Epoque grand hotels rather than an exact restoration.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the exclusive positioning.
WhataHotel notes the historic building has traditional room configurations.
